visa_products.application_channel_detail: Apply online through the official e-Visa portal, upload the required passport page and photograph, and pay any applicable fee. Apply 4–120 days before planned arrival and wait for GRANTED status before travel.
required_documents: Individual ordinary passport with at least 6 months validity when applying and at least 2 blank pages
Scanned passport biographical page
Recent front-facing photograph meeting the portal requirements
Return or onward ticket and sufficient money for the stay
Additional purpose-specific documents if taking an eligible short course, volunteering or other specialised activity
visa_products.entry_requirements: Carry the printed GRANTED e-Visa approval and the passport linked to it; if travelling on a replacement passport, also carry the old passport. Enter through a designated e-Visa airport or seaport. Have return/onward travel and sufficient funds; biometrics are captured at immigration on arrival. Complete the e-Arrival Card online within 72 hours before arrival in India at https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/earrival/. This arrival information does not replace a visa. For international arrivals by air, the Air Suvidha 2.0 health self-declaration is mandatory before immigration clearance. Complete it at https://airsuvidha.civilaviation.gov.in/ before boarding your flight, as requested by the Ministry of Civil Aviation during web check-in. The form can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival in India. Show the downloaded declaration at the International Travel Health Desk or immigration counter.
exceptions: Travellers of Pakistani origin, including the stated parental or grandparental birth/residence links, must obtain a regular visa through an Indian mission.
The e-Visa is unavailable for diplomatic/official passports or non-passport travel documents; each applicant needs an individual passport.
Applicants with a serving or retired defence, military, security or police background must use the regular-visa procedure.
Apply online at least 4 days and up to 120 days before planned arrival; wait for GRANTED status and carry the approval printout.
The 30-day e-Tourist Visa allows multiple entries within the period beginning on first arrival. The 1-year and 5-year tourist permissions have a cumulative 180-day limit per calendar year.
Entry on an e-Visa is restricted to designated airports and seaports. Biometrics are captured at immigration on arrival.
The e-Visa is non-extendable and non-convertible; protected, restricted and cantonment areas require separate permission.
If using a new passport after approval, carry the old passport on which the approval was issued as well.
Check nationality and product-specific fees. A 3% bank charge is added to applicable payable e-Visa fees.

The Ministry of Civil Aviation and Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL) today launched AIR SUVIDHA 2.0, an upgraded contactless Passenger Health Self-Declaration Portal, to strengthen public health surveillance at Points of Entry in response to the ongoing Ebola disease outbreak.

Developed in collaboration with the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, the portal enables International arriving passengers to submit a mandatory online Health Self-Declaration — covering 21-day travel history, exposure history and related symptoms, if any — prior to immigration clearance.

Airsuvidha Self Declaration Form (SDF) can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival to India. Passengers are requested to fill the forms before boarding of the flight , during web check-in for swift clearance on arrival and only required to show the downloaded SDF at the International Travel Health Desk or Immigration counter.

The form can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival in India. Show the downloaded declaration at the International Travel Health Desk or immigration counter.

The Ministry of Civil Aviation and Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL) today launched AIR SUVIDHA 2.0, an upgraded contactless Passenger Health Self-Declaration Portal, to strengthen public health surveillance at Points of Entry in response to the ongoing Ebola disease outbreak.

Developed in collaboration with the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, the portal enables International arriving passengers to submit a mandatory online Health Self-Declaration — covering 21-day travel history, exposure history and related symptoms, if any — prior to immigration clearance.

Airsuvidha Self Declaration Form (SDF) can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival to India. Passengers are requested to fill the forms before boarding of the flight , during web check-in for swift clearance on arrival and only required to show the downloaded SDF at the International Travel Health Desk or Immigration counter.

verified_elements: Complete the e-Arrival Card online within 72 hours before arrival in India at https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/earrival/. This arrival information does not replace a visa.

Complete it at https://airsuvidha.civilaviation.gov.in/ before boarding your flight, as requested by the Ministry of Civil Aviation during web check-in. The form can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival in India. Show the downloaded declaration at the International Travel Health Desk or immigration counter.

Passengers are requested to fill the forms before boarding of the flight , during web check-in for swift clearance on arrival and only required to show the downloaded SDF at the International Travel Health Desk or Immigration counter.

The Ministry of Civil Aviation and Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL) today launched AIR SUVIDHA 2.0, an upgraded contactless Passenger Health Self-Declaration Portal, to strengthen public health surveillance at Points of Entry in response to the ongoing Ebola disease outbreak.

Developed in collaboration with the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, the portal enables International arriving passengers to submit a mandatory online Health Self-Declaration — covering 21-day travel history, exposure history and related symptoms, if any — prior to immigration clearance.

Airsuvidha Self Declaration Form (SDF) can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival to India. Passengers are requested to fill the forms before boarding of the flight , during web check-in for swift clearance on arrival and only required to show the downloaded SDF at the International Travel Health Desk or Immigration counter.

verified_elements: Complete the e-Arrival Card online within 72 hours before arrival in India at https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/earrival/. This arrival information does not replace a visa.

For international arrivals by air, the Air Suvidha 2.0 health self-declaration is mandatory before immigration clearance. Complete it at https://airsuvidha.civilaviation.gov.in/ before boarding your flight, as requested by the Ministry of Civil Aviation during web check-in. The form can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival in India. Show the downloaded declaration at the International Travel Health Desk or immigration counter.

visa_products.application_channel_detail: Apply online through the official e-Visa portal, upload the required passport page and photograph, and pay any applicable fee. Apply 4–120 days before planned arrival and wait for GRANTED status before travel.
required_documents: Individual ordinary passport with at least 6 months validity when applying and at least 2 blank pages
Scanned passport biographical page
Recent front-facing photograph meeting the portal requirements
Return or onward ticket and sufficient money for the stay
Additional purpose-specific documents if taking an eligible short course, volunteering or other specialised activity
visa_products.entry_requirements: Carry the printed GRANTED e-Visa approval and the passport linked to it; if travelling on a replacement passport, also carry the old passport. Enter through a designated e-Visa airport or seaport. Have return/onward travel and sufficient funds; biometrics are captured at immigration on arrival. Complete the e-Arrival Card online within 72 hours before arrival in India at https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/earrival/. This arrival information does not replace a visa. For international arrivals by air, the Air Suvidha 2.0 health self-declaration is mandatory before immigration clearance. Complete it at https://airsuvidha.civilaviation.gov.in/ before boarding your flight, as requested by the Ministry of Civil Aviation during web check-in. The form can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival in India. Show the downloaded declaration at the International Travel Health Desk or immigration counter.
exceptions: Travellers of Pakistani origin, including the stated parental or grandparental birth/residence links, must obtain a regular visa through an Indian mission.
The e-Visa is unavailable for diplomatic/official passports or non-passport travel documents; each applicant needs an individual passport.
Applicants with a serving or retired defence, military, security or police background must use the regular-visa procedure.
Apply online at least 4 days and up to 120 days before planned arrival; wait for GRANTED status and carry the approval printout.
The 30-day e-Tourist Visa allows multiple entries within the period beginning on first arrival. The 1-year and 5-year tourist permissions have a cumulative 180-day limit per calendar year.
Entry on an e-Visa is restricted to designated airports and seaports. Biometrics are captured at immigration on arrival.
The e-Visa is non-extendable and non-convertible; protected, restricted and cantonment areas require separate permission.
If using a new passport after approval, carry the old passport on which the approval was issued as well.
Check nationality and product-specific fees. A 3% bank charge is added to applicable payable e-Visa fees.

The Ministry of Civil Aviation and Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL) today launched AIR SUVIDHA 2.0, an upgraded contactless Passenger Health Self-Declaration Portal, to strengthen public health surveillance at Points of Entry in response to the ongoing Ebola disease outbreak.

Developed in collaboration with the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, the portal enables International arriving passengers to submit a mandatory online Health Self-Declaration — covering 21-day travel history, exposure history and related symptoms, if any — prior to immigration clearance.

Airsuvidha Self Declaration Form (SDF) can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival to India. Passengers are requested to fill the forms before boarding of the flight , during web check-in for swift clearance on arrival and only required to show the downloaded SDF at the International Travel Health Desk or Immigration counter.

verified_elements: Complete the e-Arrival Card online within 72 hours before arrival in India at https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/earrival/. This arrival information does not replace a visa.

For international arrivals by air, the Air Suvidha 2.0 health self-declaration is mandatory before immigration clearance. Complete it at https://airsuvidha.civilaviation.gov.in/ before boarding your flight, as requested by the Ministry of Civil Aviation during web check-in. The form can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival in India. Show the downloaded declaration at the International Travel Health Desk or immigration counter.

For international arrivals by air, the Air Suvidha 2.0 health self-declaration is mandatory before immigration clearance. Complete it at https://airsuvidha.civilaviation.gov.in/ before boarding your flight, as requested by the Ministry of Civil Aviation during web check-in. exceptions: Visa on arrival is available only at Bangalore, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Mumbai international airports.

Eligible travellers may instead obtain the appropriate e-Visa in advance; the e-Visa has separate fees, limits and conditions.

The Ministry of Civil Aviation and Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL) today launched AIR SUVIDHA 2.0, an upgraded contactless Passenger Health Self-Declaration Portal, to strengthen public health surveillance at Points of Entry in response to the ongoing Ebola disease outbreak.

Developed in collaboration with the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, the portal enables International arriving passengers to submit a mandatory online Health Self-Declaration — covering 21-day travel history, exposure history and related symptoms, if any — prior to immigration clearance.

Airsuvidha Self Declaration Form (SDF) can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival to India. Passengers are requested to fill the forms before boarding of the flight , during web check-in for swift clearance on arrival and only required to show the downloaded SDF at the International Travel Health Desk or Immigration counter.

verified_elements: Complete the e-Arrival Card online within 72 hours before arrival in India at https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/earrival/. This arrival information does not replace a visa.

The form can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival in India. Show the downloaded declaration at the International Travel Health Desk or immigration counter.

visa_products.application_channel_detail: Apply online through the official e-Visa portal, upload the required passport page and photograph, and pay any applicable fee. Apply 4–120 days before planned arrival and wait for GRANTED status before travel.
required_documents: Individual ordinary passport with at least 6 months validity when applying and at least 2 blank pages
Scanned passport biographical page
Recent front-facing photograph meeting the portal requirements
Return or onward ticket and sufficient money for the stay
Additional purpose-specific documents if taking an eligible short course, volunteering or other specialised activity
visa_products.entry_requirements: Carry the printed GRANTED e-Visa approval and the passport linked to it; if travelling on a replacement passport, also carry the old passport. Enter through a designated e-Visa airport or seaport. Have return/onward travel and sufficient funds; biometrics are captured at immigration on arrival. Complete the e-Arrival Card online within 72 hours before arrival in India at https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/earrival/. This arrival information does not replace a visa. For international arrivals by air, the Air Suvidha 2.0 health self-declaration is mandatory before immigration clearance. Complete it at https://airsuvidha.civilaviation.gov.in/ before boarding your flight, as requested by the Ministry of Civil Aviation during web check-in. The form can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival in India. Show the downloaded declaration at the International Travel Health Desk or immigration counter.
exceptions: Travellers of Pakistani origin, including the stated parental or grandparental birth/residence links, must obtain a regular visa through an Indian mission.
The e-Visa is unavailable for diplomatic/official passports or non-passport travel documents; each applicant needs an individual passport.
Applicants with a serving or retired defence, military, security or police background must use the regular-visa procedure.
Apply online at least 4 days and up to 120 days before planned arrival; wait for GRANTED status and carry the approval printout.
The 30-day e-Tourist Visa allows multiple entries within the period beginning on first arrival. The 1-year and 5-year tourist permissions have a cumulative 180-day limit per calendar year.
Entry on an e-Visa is restricted to designated airports and seaports. Biometrics are captured at immigration on arrival.
The e-Visa is non-extendable and non-convertible; protected, restricted and cantonment areas require separate permission.
If using a new passport after approval, carry the old passport on which the approval was issued as well.
Check nationality and product-specific fees. A 3% bank charge is added to applicable payable e-Visa fees.

The Ministry of Civil Aviation and Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL) today launched AIR SUVIDHA 2.0, an upgraded contactless Passenger Health Self-Declaration Portal, to strengthen public health surveillance at Points of Entry in response to the ongoing Ebola disease outbreak.

Developed in collaboration with the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, the portal enables International arriving passengers to submit a mandatory online Health Self-Declaration — covering 21-day travel history, exposure history and related symptoms, if any — prior to immigration clearance.

Airsuvidha Self Declaration Form (SDF) can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival to India. Passengers are requested to fill the forms before boarding of the flight , during web check-in for swift clearance on arrival and only required to show the downloaded SDF at the International Travel Health Desk or Immigration counter.

verified_elements: Complete the e-Arrival Card online within 72 hours before arrival in India at https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/earrival/. This arrival information does not replace a visa.

Complete it at https://airsuvidha.civilaviation.gov.in/ before boarding your flight, as requested by the Ministry of Civil Aviation during web check-in. The form can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival in India. Show the downloaded declaration at the International Travel Health Desk or immigration counter.

The Ministry of Civil Aviation and Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL) today launched AIR SUVIDHA 2.0, an upgraded contactless Passenger Health Self-Declaration Portal, to strengthen public health surveillance at Points of Entry in response to the ongoing Ebola disease outbreak.

Developed in collaboration with the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, the portal enables International arriving passengers to submit a mandatory online Health Self-Declaration — covering 21-day travel history, exposure history and related symptoms, if any — prior to immigration clearance.

Airsuvidha Self Declaration Form (SDF) can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival to India. Passengers are requested to fill the forms before boarding of the flight , during web check-in for swift clearance on arrival and only required to show the downloaded SDF at the International Travel Health Desk or Immigration counter.

verified_elements: Complete the e-Arrival Card online within 72 hours before arrival in India at https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/earrival/. This arrival information does not replace a visa.

For international arrivals by air, the Air Suvidha 2.0 health self-declaration is mandatory before immigration clearance. Complete it at https://airsuvidha.civilaviation.gov.in/ before boarding your flight, as requested by the Ministry of Civil Aviation during web check-in. The form can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival in India. Show the downloaded declaration at the International Travel Health Desk or immigration counter.

The Ministry of Civil Aviation and Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL) today launched AIR SUVIDHA 2.0, an upgraded contactless Passenger Health Self-Declaration Portal, to strengthen public health surveillance at Points of Entry in response to the ongoing Ebola disease outbreak.

Developed in collaboration with the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, the portal enables International arriving passengers to submit a mandatory online Health Self-Declaration — covering 21-day travel history, exposure history and related symptoms, if any — prior to immigration clearance.

Airsuvidha Self Declaration Form (SDF) can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival to India. Passengers are requested to fill the forms before boarding of the flight , during web check-in for swift clearance on arrival and only required to show the downloaded SDF at the International Travel Health Desk or Immigration counter.

source_country_section.general_rule_quote: All foreign nationals entering India are required to possess a valid international travel document in the form of a national passport with a valid visa from an Indian Mission/Post or eVisa (Limited Categories) from Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs.
source_country_section.nationality_quote:
To avail e-Tourist Visa facility for Vietnam nationals, please log on to (http://indianvisaonline.gov.in) and click on the Tab/Heading “For eVisa by Bureau of Immigration".
  * Original passport (signed) + photocopy of Passport information page;
  * Photocopy of national ID card (if Vietnamese) and temporary residence card + work permit (if foreigners);
  * Photocopy of Vietnamese visa page and immigration stamp on passport (if foreigners);
  * Photocopy of air and hotel bookings (if any);
  * Undertaking forms (general undertaking, satellite, minor traveling with parents, student, journalist).
  * Note: Applicants are required to visit in person at Visa section to have their Biometrics registered. Following the visa-interview the Embassy of India could at its discretion request further documentation from the applicant (business, employment, etc.)
  * For e-Visa Application, please go to the web-link
https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/tvoa.html

Option 1: Regular Visa

  * TOURIST:

In addition to the above-mentioned documents, applicant needs to submit to the Embassy his/her bank statement in 3 months or any other financial proofs.

  * BUSINESS:

In addition to the above-mentioned documents, applicant needs to submit to the Embassy:

  * INDIA company: Invitation letter + Incorporation Certificate;
  * VIETNAM company: Decision letter + Certificate of Business Registration - all written in or translated to ENGLISH;
  * Bank statement in the last 3 months;
  * Foreigners with 2 years of continuous staying and working in Vietnam prior to application date are eligible to apply;
  * CONFERENCE:


  * Name

  * Address 

  * Phone number.

  * Email 

Checklist of documents to be submitted for Film Visa – (as required by the Missions)

Option 2: eVisa - Enabled with Electronic Travel Authorisation (TV - ETA)

  * To avail e-Tourist Visa facility for Vietnam nationals, please log on to (http://indianvisaonline.gov.in) and click on the Tab/Heading “For eVisa by Bureau of Immigration". It's a four-step process involving (i) Application online, (ii) Payment of processing fee online (iii) Receive Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) at your email ID and (iv) Fly to India with Passport and ETA.
  * e-Visa has 5 sub-categories viz. e-Tourist Visa(for 30 days/01 year/ 05 years) ,e-Business Visa, e-Medical Visa, e-Medical Attendant Visa and e-Conference Visa.
  * e-Visa fee, instructions for applicant, FAQs, payment related and other details are available in the tabs on the top-left side of the screen.

The Ministry of Civil Aviation and Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL) today launched AIR SUVIDHA 2.0, an upgraded contactless Passenger Health Self-Declaration Portal, to strengthen public health surveillance at Points of Entry in response to the ongoing Ebola disease outbreak.

Developed in collaboration with the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, the portal enables International arriving passengers to submit a mandatory online Health Self-Declaration — covering 21-day travel history, exposure history and related symptoms, if any — prior to immigration clearance.

Airsuvidha Self Declaration Form (SDF) can be completed 24 hours in advance before arrival to India. Passengers are requested to fill the forms before boarding of the flight , during web check-in for swift clearance on arrival and only required to show the downloaded SDF at the International Travel Health Desk or Immigration counter.
